content: This guidance provides a structured approach to optimizing insulin regimens for older adults with type 2 diabetes, aiming to simplify treatment while maintaining glycemic control. The recommendations include the following: 1. Adjusting the timing of basal insulin administration: Instead of administering basal insulin at bedtime, it is recommended to shift the timing to the morning. This adjustment can help streamline the regimen and potentially improve adherence. 2. Modifying basal insulin doses based on fasting glucose trends: Basal insulin should be titrated according to patterns observed in fasting blood glucose levels, ensuring that the dose is appropriate for maintaining stable glucose control. 3. Reducing or discontinuing prandial insulin when fasting glucose stabilizes: If fasting glucose levels become stable, the use of prandial (mealtime) insulin can be reduced or even discontinued. In such cases, the addition of non-insulin glucose-lowering agents may be considered to further support glycemic management. 4. Specific recommendations for individuals on premixed insulin: For patients using premixed insulin formulations, it is advised to allocate 70% of the total daily insulin dose as basal insulin in the morning. Adjustments to this regimen should be made based on individual glucose targets and clinical response. These strategies are designed to reduce the complexity of insulin regimens while ensuring effective and safe glycemic control in older adults with type 2 diabetes.
